title: Shiprocket Ltd - 544871 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Shiprocket Q2 FY27 revenue rose 35% to INR670+ crore and adjusted EBITDA hit INR14.2 crore (2.1% margin), with PAT turning positive.
summary.overview: Shiprocket reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR670 crore, up 35% YoY, with adjusted EBITDA of INR14.2 crore versus INR4 crore a year ago. Core (shipping) revenue was about INR460 crore (up 25%) at a 12.8% adjusted EBITDA margin, while Emerging (MarTech, Omnichannel, Cross-border) revenue was about INR210 crore (up 61%) with its margin improving to -21.2% from -31.5%. PAT was about INR6 million against a loss of about INR20 crore a year ago; management attributed roughly 70% of the swing to operating improvement and the rest to lower ESOP cost and post-IPO other income. Management said the core contribution margin held at about 21.1%, and that growth was volume-led rather than price-led.

segments.name: Core (shipping)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR460 crore (+25%), transactions +31%, contribution margin about INR97 crore at 21.1%, adjusted EBITDA about INR59 crore at 12.8% margin. Management says the gap between volume and revenue growth reflects courier mix, larger merchants and lower-yield hyper-local categories.

segments.name: Emerging (MarTech, Omnichannel, Cross-border)
segments.commentary: Revenue about INR210 crore (+61%), adjusted EBITDA about -INR45 crore (-21.2% margin). MarTech (rebranded Fastrr) grew 102% and powers about US$1.3 billion (about INR11,200 crore) annualised GMV; Omnichannel grew 79%; Cross-border grew 9%.

segments.name: Platform KPIs
segments.commentary: TTM transactions 233 million, TTM GMV about INR37,400 crore, over 236,000 active merchants. Quarterly GMV +33%, transactions +34%, merchants about +8%, revenue per merchant +25%. Paying active merchants reached over 2.3 lakh this quarter.

guidance_outlook: Management expects core margins to stay largely stable in the short term and improve over the longer run as fixed costs are spread over a growing base; no quarterly timeline was given.
Core operating leverage expected to be greater at the EBITDA line than at contribution margin; overhead growth to be well below revenue growth at this scale.
Q3 is seasonally weak on volume, not margin, per management; YoY there is no damage.
Management said it is largely on track for its medium-term roadmap, but gave no numeric FY27 guidance.
Finance cost and other income benefits from IPO (third week of August) reflected only about half a quarter in Q2.
capex_capacity: Shiprocket is carrier-neutral with 42+ courier partners and 250+ ecosystem partners, and owns no fleet.

AI courier selection (RADAR) routes orders by pincode and lane, and flags stressed lanes; management cited an example where 20-30 of 379 Chandigarh pincodes were stressed but under 4% of volume moved through them.
Omnichannel is investing in its own network, which keeps Emerging margins slightly lower in the short term.
Core is investing in AI, experience centres and customer acquisition; management said CAC is worthwhile if it pays back in under one year.
Agentic Analytics assistant in beta with about 1,000 users.
demand_pricing: Core yield fell roughly 4-5% (volume +31% vs revenue +25%). Management attributed this to customer mix, courier mix and lower-yield hyper-local categories, and said fuel costs were passed through rather than absorbed.
Management said growth is volume-led and not price-led; contribution margin grew faster than revenue (+43% vs +35%).
Over 90% of the business is D2C. Management said it is not changing its offering in response to supplier strategy, after a 3PL partner signalled a D2C focus.
MarTech: fewer than 10% of merchants use it; about 20,000 merchants on checkout; management claims 10-20% better conversion than the market. Competition exists in checkout.
Omnichannel: serves D2C brands with slotted replenishment to quick commerce dark stores (Blinkit, Zepto, Instamart), 97% SLA claimed, and is paid by brands rather than by quick commerce platforms.

qa_highlights.question: Are core margins (about 21.1% contribution, ~12.8% EBITDA) steady-state, and when will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Saahil Goel said margins are stable in the short term and should improve over the long run as fixed people costs are spread over more customers and ARPU. He declined to give a timeline. Tanmay Kumar said core operating leverage is greater at EBITDA than at contribution margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why did core realisation fall about 4-5% while volume grew 31%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is driven by customer-cohort mix, larger merchants and courier mix, and that fuel costs were passed through. It said the top-five-customer explanation was not what it meant and gave no exact walk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the strategy in food delivery, and is Eternal a conflict as a shareholder?
qa_highlights.answer: Restaurants are a new category using Fastrr ads, checkout and hyper-local delivery integrations, not a marketplace play. Management said Eternal is a financial investor and sees no conflict.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3PL partner's D2C push a risk to Shiprocket?
qa_highlights.answer: Saahil Goel said more than 90% of the business is D2C, that the offering will not change based on supplier preferences, and that growth trends show no visible impact.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q3 seasonality a growth or margin issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 is lower volume only, because brands shift to marketplaces during festive periods, and margins are not affected.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Emerging revenue growth sustainable, and will overhead keep falling as a share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Tanmay Kumar said MarTech growth should continue because the same decision-maker buys several products and only about 20,000 merchants use checkout. He said core overhead growth will be much lower than revenue growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why are power merchants flat or declining, and what are the unit economics of Omnichannel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said ARPU is rising and power merchants will grow as newly acquired paying merchants mature. Omnichannel customers are merchants, not quick commerce platforms, and margins are similar to logistics-style businesses.

risks_watch: Core realisation/yield trend (down about 4-5% YoY) against courier cost pass-through and mix.
Stagnant or declining power-merchant count despite merchant growth; management says it is timing, not a cap.
Competitive intensity in MarTech/checkout and dependence on carriers that may shift focus to D2C.
Core margin flat at ~21% contribution as CAC and AI investment continue; no timeline on core EBITDA margin expansion.
Q3 seasonal volume weakness and the Q3 FY27 print; watch whether PAT stays positive.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, unit economics and the Emerging trajectory, but evasive on timelines for core margin expansion and on the yield decline, deferring to 'mix' explanations without quantification.
key_quotes: Our merchants do not need to worry about logistics. She just needs to make a great product, and we’ll take care of everything else.
So long as our CAC pays back in less than one year, it is a beneficial investment to do.
Fuel pricing did get passed on more or less. Like I said, we do not absorb it, and that shows up in the contribution margin, right?
I do not think you should infer at all that the top five are doing better.

growth.why: No numeric FY27 guidance; management says it is on track for its medium-term roadmap, with core margins stable and operating leverage expected over the longer run, and Q2 revenue grew 35% YoY on volume-led growth (transactions +31-34%), but no capacity additions or order book were quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Core contribution margin held at about 21.1% and core EBITDA margin at 12.8% (vs 12.4% a year ago), with management saying margins are stable short term and improve long run, but no timeline was given.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Shiprocket is carrier-neutral with 42+ courier partners and owns no fleet, and no new capacity came live or was dated in the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Quarterly GMV grew 33%, transactions 34% and core transactions 31%, with Q3 seasonally weaker on volume but with no YoY damage per management.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is not discussed; the company is asset-light, and the call only mentions investment in AI, experience centres and CAC and Omnichannel's own network.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gave no numeric FY27 guidance and only said it is on track for its medium-term roadmap, so there is no explicit guide to raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Core yield fell about 4-5% while volume grew 31%, and Q3 is seasonally weak on volume, with a 3PL partner signalling a D2C focus as a watch item.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Agentic Analytics assistant is in beta with about 1,000 users and restaurants are a new Emerging category using Fastrr ads, checkout and hyper-local integrations, but no launch date was given.

rows.label: Emerging segment growth continuing
rows.why: Emerging revenue grew 61% YoY to about INR210 crore, MarTech grew 102% and powers about US$1.3 billion annualised GMV, and management says growth should continue as the same buyer purchases several products with only about 20,000 merchants on checkout.

rows.label: Overhead leverage in core
rows.why: Management expects core overhead growth to stay well below revenue growth, and core EBITDA margin rose to 12.8% from 12.4% a year ago with Emerging EBITDA margin improving from -31.5% to -21.2%.

rows.label: Core yield pressure
rows.why: Core yield fell roughly 4-5% (volume +31% vs revenue +25%) on courier and customer mix and lower-yield hyper-local categories, with management giving no exact walk and fuel costs passed through.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume growth, Emerging trajectory and unit economics, but cautious on core margin timing and gave only mix explanations for the 4-5% yield decline, which analysts pressed on.
